story: Wire Codex Adapter to Session Orchestration
story_description: As a developer, I need the Codex adapter components wired into SessionOrchestrator and EngineManager so that Codex sessions use long-lived stdio processes instead of spawn-per-turn like Claude.
task_description: Modify SessionOrchestrator.executeTurn() to detect the session provider type and route Codex sessions to a shared long-lived CodexStdioAdapter instance per workspace, while Claude sessions continue using spawn-per-turn. Add codexThreadId and codexWorkspaceId fields to Session model. Update EngineManager to return appropriate adapter type based on provider.
atom_description: SessionOrchestrator.executeTurn() detects provider type from session. For Codex sessions, it uses a shared CodexStdioAdapter per workspace (long-lived process). For Claude sessions, it continues spawn-per-turn pattern. Session model gains codexThreadId and codexWorkspaceId optional fields. EngineRouter returns CodexStdioAdapter for .codex engine type. Includes process lifecycle management: start on first turn, reuse across turns, cleanup on session end.
problem_statement: Even with all Codex adapter components (CodexStdioAdapter, CodexEventMapper, CodexResponseParser) implemented, they are not wired into the Blaze session flow. SessionOrchestrator currently hardcodes Claude adapter usage. Codex CLI uses a fundamentally different interaction model: long-lived stdio process with JSON-RPC vs Claude spawn-per-turn with NDJSON. Without this wiring, Codex sessions cannot execute turns.

notes: This atom is the integration glue that makes Codex sessions work end-to-end. It bridges the gap between individual adapter components and the session orchestration layer. Key insight: Codex uses long-lived stdio process while Claude spawns per turn, requiring different adapter lifecycle management.
